canonical_name: Dijkstra single-source shortest-path algorithm family (repository method label)
source_attribution: Edsger Dijkstra, 1959 (catalog metadata; primary paper lead inspected separately)
statement_blocker: The repository fixes no graph representation, weight domain or nonnegativity predicate, reachability and unreachable-value convention, algorithm state, relaxation and tie semantics, termination measure, output contract, or complexity model. The inspected 1959 source states a one-pair minimum-path problem and constructs paths from P until Q is reached, whereas the catalog uses a modern single-source gloss. Selecting one-pair correctness, all-distance correctness, predecessor-tree correctness, total implementation correctness, or a complexity theorem would introduce proposition-changing choices without an approved source transport.
target_decision: retain the recognizable Dijkstra family and require an independently reviewed immutable-source proposition and source-to-modern-scope transport before statement execution
domain_and_universes: Open: an approved source target must fix the finite vertex carrier and graph/quiver representation, edge identity and direction, weight type and algebra/order structures, source and optional target, path/walk and reachability encodings, algorithm state and result type, and all universe/typeclass context.
conclusion: Open: the repository does not choose one-pair minimum-path correctness, all-reachable-vertex distance correctness, predecessor-tree correctness, termination and total correctness of a particular implementation, or a resource bound.
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded before a proposition is selected; every graph-size, reachability, source-target, zero/negative weight, tie, cycle, duplicate-path, arithmetic, and early-stop case in scope-map.md requires a source-mapped decision.
candidate_scope_not_credited: correctness for Dijkstra's 1959 source-target procedure under the paper's global path-existence premise
correctness of distance and predecessor labels for every vertex reachable from one source
an extended-distance formulation assigning infinity to unreachable vertices
termination and total correctness of a specified executable priority-queue implementation
a complexity bound under a specified graph representation, queue, arithmetic, and cost model
excluded_substitutions: minimum-spanning-tree Problem 1 from the same 1959 paper
generic shortest-path existence or an unweighted graph-distance theorem
Quiver.shortestPath edge-count minimization presented as Dijkstra algorithm correctness
Bellman-Ford, Floyd-Warshall, A-star, or another shortest-path algorithm
a structure field or hypothesis assuming the desired distances, paths, invariant, or correctness
one numerical execution, benchmark, trace, floating-point result, or unchecked certificate
